translation_en: Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us: Thabit al-Bunani narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Rabah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Delegations came to Mu'awiyah during Ramadan, and we used to prepare food for one another. Abu Hurayrah often invited us to his lodging, so I thought: Why should I not prepare food and invite them to my lodging? I ordered food to be prepared. In the evening I met Abu Hurayrah and said: The invitation is at my place tonight. He said: You got ahead of me. I said: Yes. I invited them. Abu Hurayrah said: People of the Ansar, shall I tell you a hadith from your own history? Then he mentioned the conquest of Makkah. He said: The Messenger of Allah advanced until he reached Makkah. He placed al-Zubayr in command of one flank, Khalid in command of the other flank, and Abu 'Ubaydah in command of the unarmored infantry. They took the bottom of the valley, while the Messenger of Allah was with a detachment. He looked and saw me, and said: Abu Hurayrah! I said: At your service, Messenger of Allah. He said: Let no one come to me except an Ansari. A narrator other than Shayban adds that he said: Call the Ansar to me. They gathered around him. Quraysh had gathered their rabble and followers. They said: We will send these people forward; if they gain anything, we will join them, but if they are struck, we will give what is asked of us. The Messenger of Allah said: Do you see the rabble of Quraysh and their followers? He placed one hand over the other and said: Until you meet me at al-Safa. We set out. Whoever among us wanted to kill one of them was able to do so, and none of them turned anything against us. Abu Sufyan came and said: Messenger of Allah, the green force of Quraysh has been made lawful to kill; there will be no Quraysh after today. Then the Prophet said: Whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house is safe. Some of the Ansar said to one another: The man has been overcome by longing for his town and compassion for his clan. Abu Hurayrah said: Revelation came. When revelation came, it was never hidden from us; when it came, no one raised his eyes toward the Messenger of Allah until it had ended. When revelation ended, the Messenger of Allah said: People of the Ansar! They said: At your service, Messenger of Allah. He said: Did you say: The man has been overcome by longing for his town? They said: That did happen. He said: No. I am Allah's servant and Messenger. I emigrated to Allah and to you. My life is with you and my death is with you. They came toward him weeping and saying: By Allah, we said what we said only out of attachment to Allah and His Messenger. The Messenger of Allah said: Allah and His Messenger affirm what you say and excuse you. The people went toward Abu Sufyan's house, and others closed their doors. The Messenger of Allah came to the Black Stone, touched it, and circumambulated the House. He came upon an idol beside the House that they used to worship. In the Messenger of Allah's hand was a bow, and he held its curved end. When he came to the idol, he began thrusting at its eye and saying: The truth has come and falsehood has vanished. When he finished his circumambulation, he went to al-Safa, climbed it until he could see the House, raised his hands, praised Allah, and supplicated as he wished.
